events.title: Elizabeth Blackwell earns her medical degree
events.summary: She becomes the first woman physician trained in America.
events.description: On January 23, 1849, Elizabeth Blackwell received an MD degree from Geneva Medical College in New York, becoming the first American-trained woman physician.
events.notificationBody: In 1849, Elizabeth Blackwell became America's first woman medical graduate.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 23

events.title: The Shaanxi earthquake strikes China
events.summary: An estimated 830,000 people are killed or injured.
events.description: On January 23, 1556, an earthquake centered in Shaanxi province, China, killed or injured an estimated 830,000 people.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 23

events.title: Madeleine Albright becomes US secretary of state
events.summary: She is the first woman to hold the post.
events.description: On January 23, 1997, Madeleine Albright became US secretary of state, the first woman to hold that cabinet post.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 23

events.title: The Twenty-fourth Amendment bans poll taxes
events.summary: The amendment ends poll taxes in federal elections.
events.description: On January 23, 1964, the Twenty-fourth Amendment to the US Constitution was ratified, prohibiting poll taxes as a condition of voting in federal elections.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 23

events.title: Gold is discovered in California
events.summary: James Marshall's find at Sutter's Mill sets off the Gold Rush.
events.description: On January 24, 1848, James Marshall spotted gold while building a sawmill in California, a discovery that set off the California Gold Rush.
events.notificationBody: In 1848, gold was found in California, setting off the Gold Rush.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 24

events.title: Apple introduces the Macintosh
events.summary: Steve Jobs unveils Apple's new personal computer.
events.description: On January 24, 1984, Steve Jobs introduced Apple's Macintosh computer.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 24

events.title: Winston Churchill dies
events.summary: Britain's wartime prime minister dies in London.
events.description: On January 24, 1965, Winston Churchill, Britain's prime minister during most of World War II, died.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 24

events.title: Edith Wharton is born
events.summary: The novelist of New York society is born.
events.description: On January 24, 1862, Edith Wharton, an American author best known for her stories and novels about upper-class society, was born in New York.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 24

events.title: The first Winter Olympics open in Chamonix
events.summary: About 250 athletes from 16 countries gather in the French Alps.
events.description: On January 25, 1924, the first Winter Olympic Games opened in Chamonix, France. Some 250 athletes from 16 countries competed in 16 events; the games were originally staged as an International Winter Sports Week.
events.notificationBody: In 1924, the first Winter Olympics opened in Chamonix, France.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Chamonix 1924 Olympic Winter Games

events.title: Jesuit missionaries found Sao Paulo
events.summary: The settlement will grow into Brazil's largest city.
events.description: On January 25, 1554, Jesuit missionaries founded the city of Sao Paulo in Brazil.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 25

events.title: Robert Burns is born
events.summary: Scotland's national poet is born.
events.description: On January 25, 1759, Robert Burns, the national poet of Scotland, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 25

events.title: Virginia Woolf is born in London
events.summary: The modernist novelist is born.
events.description: On January 25, 1882, the novelist Virginia Woolf was born in London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 25

events.title: Mass protests begin in Egypt
events.summary: Demonstrators clash with police in Cairo and other cities.
events.description: On January 25, 2011, demonstrators in Cairo and several other Egyptian cities clashed with police, the start of mass protests against the government.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 25

events.title: The Cullinan diamond is found
events.summary: The world's largest diamond is discovered at the Premier Mine in South Africa.
events.description: On January 26, 1905, the largest diamond ever found, weighing more than a pound, was discovered at the Premier Mine in South Africa.
events.notificationTitle: A diamond weighing over a pound
events.notificationBody: In 1905, the record-breaking Cullinan diamond was found in South Africa.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 26

events.title: India becomes a republic
events.summary: The new constitution takes effect.
events.description: On January 26, 1950, India became a republic, achieving full independence from Great Britain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 26

events.title: Arthur Phillip founds the first British settlement in Australia
events.summary: The British flag is raised at Sydney Cove.
events.description: On January 26, 1788, Arthur Phillip hoisted the British flag at Sydney Cove and established the first permanent European settlement in Australia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 26

events.title: A major earthquake strikes Gujarat, India
events.summary: The quake near Bhuj kills more than 20,000 people.
events.description: On January 26, 2001, a major earthquake struck near Bhuj in Gujarat, India, killing more than 20,000 people.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 26

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera opens on Broadway
events.summary: Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical opens in New York.
events.description: On January 26, 1988, The Phantom of the Opera opened in New York City.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 26

events.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is born
events.summary: The composer is born in Salzburg.
events.description: On January 27, 1756, the composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Salzburg.
events.notificationBody: In 1756, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Salzburg.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 27
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

events.title: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz
events.summary: Soldiers find about 7,650 surviving prisoners at the Nazi camp.
events.description: On January 27, 1945, Soviet troops arrived at Auschwitz, the Nazi concentration and extermination camp near Oswiecim in Poland, and found 7,650 sick and starving prisoners. Between 1.1 and 1.5 million people died there.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Auschwitz

events.title: The Siege of Leningrad ends
events.summary: The Red Army lifts the 872-day blockade.
events.description: On January 27, 1944, the Soviet Red Army drove German and Finnish forces from the Leningrad area, ending an 872-day siege.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 27

events.title: The Paris Peace Accords are signed
events.summary: The agreements formally end the Vietnam War.
events.description: On January 27, 1973, the Paris Peace Accords formally ending the Vietnam War were signed.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 27

events.title: Dante is exiled from Florence
events.summary: The poet's political enemies banish him.
events.description: On January 27, 1302, the Italian poet Dante Alighieri was exiled from Florence by his political enemies.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 27

events.title: The LEGO brick patent is filed
events.summary: The interlocking toy brick goes on to conquer the world.
events.description: On January 28, 1958, the patent for the LEGO toy building brick was filed. The brick became hugely popular around the world.
events.notificationBody: In 1958, LEGO filed the patent for its famous interlocking brick.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 28

events.title: The space shuttle Challenger is lost
events.summary: The shuttle breaks apart 73 seconds after liftoff.
events.description: On January 28, 1986, the US space shuttle Challenger exploded 73 seconds after liftoff from Florida, killing all seven crew members.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 28

events.title: Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice is published
events.summary: The novel enjoys immediate success.
events.description: On January 28, 1813, Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice was published and enjoyed immediate success.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 28

events.title: Charlemagne dies
events.summary: The first emperor of the revived Western empire dies at Aachen.
events.description: On January 28, 814, Charlemagne, ruler of the Franks and emperor in the West since 800, died.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 28

events.title: Paris falls after a four-month siege
events.summary: The French capital capitulates in the Franco-German War.
events.description: On January 28, 1871, Paris fell to German forces following a four-month siege during the Franco-German War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 28

events.title: Karl Benz patents his motorcar
events.summary: The first practical gasoline-powered automobile is patented.
events.description: On January 29, 1886, Karl Benz patented the first practical automobile powered by an internal-combustion engine.
events.notificationBody: In 1886, Karl Benz patented his motorcar.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 29

events.title: Poe's 'The Raven' is first published
events.summary: 'Nevermore' enters American literature.
events.description: On January 29, 1845, Edgar Allan Poe's poem 'The Raven' was first published.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 29

events.title: Anton Chekhov is born
events.dateNote: January 17 in the Julian calendar then used in Russia.
events.summary: The Russian playwright and short-story master is born.
events.description: On January 29, 1860, the Russian playwright and short-story writer Anton Chekhov was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 29

events.title: Baseball's Hall of Fame elects its first players
events.summary: Babe Ruth and Ty Cobb are among the first inductees chosen.
events.description: On January 29, 1936, Babe Ruth and Ty Cobb were among the first players elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 29

events.title: The Beatles play together for the last time
events.summary: The band's final live performance takes place on a London rooftop.
events.description: On January 30, 1969, the Beatles, John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr, performed together in public for the last time.
events.notificationBody: In 1969, the Beatles performed together in public for the last time.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 30

events.title: Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated
events.summary: India's independence leader is killed in New Delhi.
events.description: On January 30, 1948, Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated by the Hindu extremist Nathuram Godse.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 30

events.title: Charles I of England is executed
events.dateNote: Julian calendar date; contemporary English records gave the year as 1648.
events.summary: The king is beheaded in London after the English Civil Wars.
events.description: On January 30, 1649, Charles I of England was executed in London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 30

events.title: Adolf Hitler is named chancellor of Germany
events.summary: President Hindenburg appoints the Nazi leader.
events.description: On January 30, 1933, German President Paul von Hindenburg named Adolf Hitler chancellor of Germany.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 30

events.title: Charlie Chaplin's City Lights premieres
events.summary: The silent comedy is often called Chaplin's crowning achievement.
events.description: On January 30, 1931, Charlie Chaplin's City Lights had its world premiere. It is often considered his crowning achievement.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 30

events.title: The United Kingdom leaves the European Union
events.summary: Brexit takes effect more than three years after the referendum.
events.description: On January 31, 2020, the United Kingdom formally left the European Union, more than three years after voting to leave.
events.notificationTitle: Britain steps out of the EU
events.notificationBody: In 2020, the United Kingdom formally left the European Union.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 31

events.title: Franz Schubert is born near Vienna
events.summary: The Austrian composer is born.
events.description: On January 31, 1797, the composer Franz Schubert was born near Vienna.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 31

events.title: Friedrich Paulus surrenders at Stalingrad
events.summary: The German field marshal surrenders to the Red Army.
events.description: On January 31, 1943, German Field Marshal Friedrich Paulus surrendered to the Soviet Red Army at Stalingrad.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 31

events.title: Jackie Robinson is born
events.summary: The player who will break baseball's color line is born.
events.description: On January 31, 1919, Jackie Robinson was born. He became the first African American to play in baseball's major leagues in the 20th century.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 31

events.title: Guy Fawkes is executed in London
events.summary: The Gunpowder Plot conspirator is put to death.
events.description: On January 31, 1606, Guy Fawkes was executed in London for his role in the Gunpowder Plot.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 31
